To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uncertainty in the thermal conductivity and the specific heat of structural elements affects the accuracy of energy simulations of residential buildings in a different way.

the uncertainty in thermal conductivity and specific heats of structural layers affects the heating and cooling energy demand in different ways depending on the climatic conditions and the building features, and the uncertainty of the thermal conductivity is more relevant in the heating needs while the specific heat is more important in the cooling needs.

the propagation of uncertainty of the thermal conductivity of structural layers is more significant than that of the specific heat in the estimation of the annual heating and that the uncertainty of the specific heat is more relevant in cooling needs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of those building characteristics that are critical in the uncertainty propagation analysis of energy simulation.
the identification of building features and their combinations that are more sensitive to the uncertainty propagation of material properties.

the influence of buildings features on the propagation of uncertainties in the energy simulation of existing buildings, which is an important aspect to be taken into account for the development of reliable energy retrofit strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the propagation of uncertainty depends on both the building features and the climate conditions.
the influence of the uncertainty in the thermal properties of the building components is not only related to the thermal insulation of the envelope but also to the building geometry and orientation.

the uncertainty in thermal conductivity and specific thermal capacity of building components affects the accuracy of building energy performance in a way that is strictly correlated with the building configuration and with the local climate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the influence of the uncertainty in material properties depends on both building and climatic features.
the uncertainty propagation of material properties is highly dependent on the building configuration and the climate.

the uncertainty in the thermal conductivity of the structural layers affects mostly the heating and cooling loads estimation in the buildings with a low and high aspect ratio, respectively, while the uncertainty in the specific heat of the structural layers influences more the heating needs in buildings with an external insulation and the cooling needs in buildings with internal insulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainty in material properties can have a large effect on building energy needs and that the effect of this uncertainty is strongly influenced by the building features.
the uncertainty in material properties is not a random effect but it can be reduced by considering the specific features of each building.
the uncertainty in the estimation of annual heating and cooling demands is highly affected by the building features.
